annotations.title: Trace duct circuits from one part and compute their pressure drop

description:
THE CIRCUITS A FAN IS SIZED ON, AND THEIR PRESSURE DROP, without
anyone clicking.

Give ONE part - an air handling unit, a fan, a duct - and this walks
the whole network it belongs to. It then keeps ONE CIRCUIT PER BRANCH
leaving that part: the longest path in metres of each branch. From an
air handling unit, that is one circuit per network connected to it -
supply, return, intake, exhaust.

EACH OF THESE CIRCUITS IS COMPUTED, and becomes a circuit of the
model: it has a name, a COLOUR, and a tab on the website.

WHAT YOU GET
  circuits        one per branch: name, colour, length, and - once
                  'etat' is 'pret' - the pressure drop in Pa, its
                  linear and local parts, the maximum velocity, the
                  flow used at the start and where it came from.
  autres_arrivees shorter paths, found but NOT computed.
  lien_3d         the page where every circuit shows in its colour.
  metre           the take-off of the whole network.

IF A CIRCUIT IS STILL 'calcul', call again with THE SAME ARGUMENTS a
moment later. Nothing is recomputed: an identical call only reads.
A different velocity or flow is applied to the circuits already
there, without a new analysis.

HOW TO USE IT WELL.

Ask the user for the design velocity before calling, or say which one
you used. THIS TOOL DOES NOT READ THE FLOW FROM THE MODEL: look for
it in the air handling unit's properties with read_ifc_overview and
pass it as flow_m3h - see that argument. Failing that, the flow is
the design velocity times the section of the first straight duct.
Say which of the two it was with every figure - the pressure drop is a first
estimate the user must correct, never a fan sizing.

Every circuit is computed as a SUPPLY circuit until someone says
otherwise: the tool cannot tell supply from return. The flow rates do
not depend on it - a duct carries what its section allows either
way - but the tee coefficients and the design velocity do. If a
branch is a return, an intake or an exhaust, SAY SO and tell the user
how to set it in the 3D view: hovering the arrow of a circuit shows
its type, and each click on that label moves to the next one -
supply, return, outdoor air, exhaust. A click on the arrow itself
reverses the air direction, which is how the user says at which end
the terminal or the louvre sits when the duct has a constant section.

Say that each circuit was chosen BY LENGTH. A shorter path loaded
with dampers, bends or silencers can lose more pressure.

ALWAYS GIVE THE USER THE 3D LINK, and name the circuits by their
colour. On that page the user can delete a circuit from its tab -
its colour goes with it - add one by clicking a start and an end
part, correct a flow rate, and download the workbook, one sheet per
circuit.

THE USER'S CHOICES STAND. A circuit they deleted is not computed
again: it comes back under 'retires_par_l_utilisateur', and only they
can restore it, by tracing it on the page. A circuit they traced by
hand is never replaced. So after they have been on the page, call
this again before stating any figure - never answer from memory.

excluded_guids.description: Parts to close, by GlobalId. Closing a part cuts the walk there: whatever was only reached through it leaves the survey. Use it when the network visibly runs too far - through a plenum shared with another installation, for instance.
excluded_guids.title: Excluded Guids

flow_m3h.description: Flow rate at the starting part, m3/h. It CAPS the flow of every circuit leaving that part; it does not set it. BEFORE GUESSING, LOOK FOR IT: run read_ifc_overview and read the properties of the air handling unit, the fan or the casing you are starting from - a field named Debit, Flow, Air Flow, Luftmenge or Portata, often under a flow property set. Pass what you find, say where it came from, and convert it to m3/h (a value in m3/s is 3600 times smaller). If the model carries nothing, ASK THE USER rather than inventing one. Omit it only when nobody knows: the flow is then derived from the design velocity and the section of the first straight duct.
flow_m3h.title: Flow M3H

max_velocity_m_s.description: Design velocity, in m/s, 0.5 to 12. It sets the flow rate at the start of each circuit when flow_m3h is not given (velocity x section of the first straight duct), and the flow after each branch. Ventilation: 4 to 6 in main ducts, 2 to 3 near the terminals. ASK THE USER rather than guessing. Omit: the model default, 5 m/s.
max_velocity_m_s.title: Max Velocity M S

start_guid.description: GlobalId of the part to start from: an air handling unit, a fan, or any duct of the network. Take it from read_ifc_overview (guid_exemple) or from read_ifc_networks.
start_guid.title: Start Guid

token.description: The model token, from ifc_upload_result or from the link the user pasted.
token.title: Token
